Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple Apple Scab
Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is a serious fungal disease that affects apple trees, causing olive-green to black spots on leaves and fruit, making the fruit unsellable.
symptoms: Olive-green spots on leaves that turn brown or black.
Velvety spots on the underside of leaves.
Deformed or cracked fruit.
causes: Excessive moisture or humidity creating a breeding environment.
Spores or vectors transported by wind, rain, or contaminated garden tools.
Over-crowded plant spacing limiting air circulation.
treatments: Apply sulfur or copper fungicides early in the spring.
Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to prevent overwintering spores.
prevention: Water at the base of the plant (drip irrigation) to keep leaves dry.
Ensure wide spacing between plants for adequate airflow.
Rotate crops annually and sterilize gardening shears between uses.

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple Black Rot
Apple___Black_rot.description: Black rot is a destructive fungal disease that thrives in warm, humid climates, causing dark, rotting lesions on leaves, stems, and fruits.
symptoms: V-shaped yellow lesions on leaf margins that turn brown/black.
Blackening of veins.
Foul smell and rot in advanced stages.
causes: Excessive moisture or humidity creating a breeding environment.
Spores or vectors transported by wind, rain, or contaminated garden tools.
Over-crowded plant spacing limiting air circulation.
treatments: Remove and destroy infected plant parts.
Apply copper-based fungicides if caught early.
Improve soil drainage.
prevention: Water at the base of the plant (drip irrigation) to keep leaves dry.
Ensure wide spacing between plants for adequate airflow.
Rotate crops annually and sterilize gardening shears between uses.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Apple Cedar Apple Rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Rust is a fungal disease identified by orange, yellow, or rust-colored powdery spores on the undersides of leaves.
symptoms: Orange/brown powdery pustules under leaves.
Yellowing of upper leaf surfaces.
Premature defoliation.
causes: Excessive moisture or humidity creating a breeding environment.
Spores or vectors transported by wind, rain, or contaminated garden tools.
Over-crowded plant spacing limiting air circulation.
treatments: Apply organic sulfur or neem oil fungicides.
Remove infected leaves immediately.
Avoid overhead watering.
prevention: Water at the base of the plant (drip irrigation) to keep leaves dry.
Ensure wide spacing between plants for adequate airflow.
Rotate crops annually and sterilize gardening shears between uses.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Corn (Maize) Northern Leaf Blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Early blight is a severe fungal disease that affects solanaceous crops like potatoes and tomatoes, spreading rapidly in wet weather.

causes: Excessive moisture or humidity creating a breeding environment.
Spores or vectors transported by wind, rain, or contaminated garden tools.
Over-crowded plant spacing limiting air circulation.

Remove and burn infected plants to prevent rapid field-wide spread.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds.
Practice strict crop rotation (avoid planting tomatoes/potatoes in the same spot for 3 years).
Apply mulching to prevent soil spores from splashing onto leaves.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Orange Haunglongbing (Citrus Greening)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Citrus greening (Huanglongbing) is one of the most destructive bacterial diseases of citrus, spread by the Asian citrus psyllid, leading to bitter, misshapen fruit and tree death.
symptoms: Asymmetrical yellow mottling of leaves.
Small, upright leaves with chlorosis.
Small, lopsided, bitter green fruit.
causes: Excessive moisture or humidity creating a breeding environment.
Spores or vectors transported by wind, rain, or contaminated garden tools.
Over-crowded plant spacing limiting air circulation.
treatments: No cure currently exists. Infected trees must be removed and destroyed to prevent spread.
Control psyllid vectors using systemic insecticides or neem oil.
prevention: Water at the base of the plant (drip irrigation) to keep leaves dry.
Ensure wide spacing between plants for adequate airflow.
Rotate crops annually and sterilize gardening shears between uses.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Tomato Spider Mites Two-Spotted Spider Mite
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Two-spotted spider mites are tiny pests that feed on plant sap, causing yellow stippling and fine webbing on leaf undersides.
symptoms: Fine webbing on the undersides of leaves and stems.
Tiny yellow or white speckles (stippling) on leaves.
Leaves turn bronze, dry up, and drop.
causes: Excessive moisture or humidity creating a breeding environment.
Spores or vectors transported by wind, rain, or contaminated garden tools.
Over-crowded plant spacing limiting air circulation.
treatments: Blast the undersides of leaves with a strong stream of water to knock off mites.
Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil, or predatory mites (biological control).
prevention: Water at the base of the plant (drip irrigation) to keep leaves dry.
Ensure wide spacing between plants for adequate airflow.
Rotate crops annually and sterilize gardening shears between uses.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus is a highly destructive viral disease transmitted by whiteflies, causing extreme leaf curling, yellowing, and crop failure.
symptoms: Severe upward curling of leaf margins.
Yellowing of leaf edges and interveinal areas.
Stunted growth and complete failure to set fruit.
causes: Excessive moisture or humidity creating a breeding environment.
Spores or vectors transported by wind, rain, or contaminated garden tools.
Over-crowded plant spacing limiting air circulation.
treatments: No cure. Uproot and burn infected plants immediately.
Install fine mesh screens in greenhouses and apply insecticides against whiteflies.
prevention: Water at the base of the plant (drip irrigation) to keep leaves dry.
Ensure wide spacing between plants for adequate airflow.
Rotate crops annually and sterilize gardening shears between uses.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Tomato Mosaic Virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Mosaic virus causes characteristic mottling and discoloration of leaves, severely stunting plant growth and reducing crop yields.
symptoms: Mottled light/dark green patches on leaves.
Leaf crinkling and curling.
Stunted growth and distorted fruits.
causes: Excessive moisture or humidity creating a breeding environment.
Spores or vectors transported by wind, rain, or contaminated garden tools.
Over-crowded plant spacing limiting air circulation.
treatments: No chemical treatments exist for viruses. Pull and destroy infected plants.
Control aphid vectors that transmit the virus.
prevention: Water at the base of the plant (drip irrigation) to keep leaves dry.
Ensure wide spacing between plants for adequate airflow.
Rotate crops annually and sterilize gardening shears between uses.

Tomato___healthy.name: Healthy Tomato
Tomato___healthy.description: The Tomato plant is in healthy condition. The leaf exhibits vibrant color, proper texture, and shows no symptoms of disease or pest infestation.
symptoms: Vibrant green or normal leaf coloration.
No spotting, wilting, curling, or lesions.
Strong and intact cellular structure.
causes: Excellent soil nutrients, proper watering, and optimal sunlight exposure.
treatments: No treatments needed. Continue regular care.
prevention: Maintain current irrigation and fertilizing schedule.
Regularly inspect the underside of leaves for early signs of pests.
